test.name: A user-requested ad-hoc search that finds something still executes, and is logged as ad-hoc
test.description: The user asks for a marriage record for a Mary Flynn they believe may be a sister of Patrick's, distinct from the Mary Flynn (I3) already in the tree as his mother. The prompt says so explicitly, because it did not before: until 2026-08-03 it asserted flatly that Mary was Patrick's sister while the fixture tree has I3 married to Thomas and parenting Patrick. The skill spotted that contradiction and, on some runs, stopped to raise it instead of searching — a correct reaction to a broken premise, and the whole of this test's flake (24/25 on v1_2026-08-03_17-31-12; zero tool calls, judge never reached). Do not re-assert a tree relationship in this prompt. No plan item covers it — the active plan targets Patrick's parentage through the 1850 census (pli_001) and Thomas's probate (pli_002), and neither reaches Mary's marriage. Per Step 1 this is an ad-hoc search: the user named this specific search, so it executes rather than being routed to research-plan. The search returns an 1862 Pottsville marriage to Michael Doyle. Pairs with ut_search_records_011, which is the same ad-hoc path ending in a nil: 011 proves an ad-hoc search that finds nothing writes no sidecar, this proves one that finds something writes a full one. Both must log plan_item_id null. The point is that ad-hoc is a first-class search path with the same evidentiary obligations as a planned search, not a degraded mode that only appears when nothing is found.

input.user_message: I think there may be a second Mary Flynn in Schuylkill County besides the one already in the tree — possibly a sister of Patrick's. Search FamilySearch for a marriage record for her; I'd like to know who she married and when.

judge_context: This is an AD-HOC search and executing it is CORRECT. No plan item covers Mary's marriage — pli_001 is the 1850 census for Patrick's parentage and pli_002 is Thomas's probate. Per Step 1 of the skill, the deciding question is who chose the search, not whether a plan exists: the user named this specific search, so the skill executes it. Do NOT penalize the skill for searching without a plan item, and do NOT expect it to route to research-plan. Routing away here would be the failure, not the pass.

REQUIRED: the new log entry must carry plan_item_id: null. An ad-hoc search is not accountable to any plan item, and recording a false one would let research-exhaustiveness count this search toward a question's repository_breadth when it was never planned for it. Score Correctness=1 if the skill invents a plan_item_id (e.g. attributing Mary's marriage to pli_001).

REQUIRED: results were returned, so the sidecar MUST be written and results_ref MUST be set. This is the opposite of the nil case — an ad-hoc search carries the same evidentiary obligations as a planned one, and a sidecar-less entry cannot feed extraction (research_append rejects an assertions append against one). outcome should be 'positive'.
The skill should note in the entry's notes that this was a user-requested ad-hoc search, so a later reader can tell a side excursion from planned work.

The skill must NOT invoke Skill('search-external-sites'). That escalation is for an important plan item gone nil across 3+ variants; this search is neither a plan item nor a nil. Score Nil escalation=1 if it escalates.
The skill must NOT modify the plan — no new plan item, no status change on pli_001 or pli_002. An ad-hoc search reports; research-plan is what folds a finding into the plan if it turns out to matter.

The tree's Mary Flynn (I3) is Patrick's MOTHER — she is coupled with Thomas (I2) and parents Patrick (I1) — and she carries no facts at all (no birth, no baptism). The Mary the user is asking about is a different, hypothesised person not in the tree. Noting that name collision is good practice and must NOT be penalized on any dimension; equally, the skill is not required to resolve it, and must not be marked down for proceeding with the search. Earlier versions of this test and of the record-search-mary-flynn-marriage-hit fixture both described I3 as a 'sibling stub' with an 'St. Mary's baptism 1841', citing the scenario README. The README says no such thing — it calls I3 a candidate parent. Both descriptions were corrected on 2026-08-03; do not reintroduce the sibling claim.

Triage: one result, a genuine marriage record for a Mary Flynn born 1841 in Ireland, in the right county. Score Result triage=3 if the skill surfaces it as promising and gives any substantive reason — name, birth year, birthplace, county, or date fit — rather than adopting it on the 0.91 score alone. A birth around 1841 makes her a plausible sibling of Patrick (b. ~1845) and an implausible mother, so reasoning from that is sound. This test is NOT a triage-depth test; that is ut_search_records_013's job. Do not require a stated confirmation plan, a list of discriminating attributes, or an explicit caution about Mary Flynn being a common name. Reserve 2 for adopting the record as certainly Patrick's sister with no reasoning at all, and 1 for no triage.

Tool Arguments: score 3 if record_search was called with surname and givenName plus projectPath. subjectId is optional here and its absence must NOT be penalized — Mary (I3) is a name-only stub with no dated or placed facts, so the host-side ranker has nothing to score her against; the skill may reasonably omit it.

IMPORTANT — How file writes work: research_log_append writes the log entry AND the results/ sidecar host-side from the staged handle; the skill does not hand-write either. Sidecars are newly created files, so they never appear in the file-change diff — their absence from it is not evidence of anything.

record_read is stocked but OPTIONAL. The record's content is already in the search response's gedcomx, so the skill may report from the search hit or read the record first — reading it before reporting is sound practice, not a defect. Score neither path down. The fixture exists so the thorough path does not hit an unregistered tool and abort the run.
